about: The Act Directory (STATUTE_COVERAGE_PLAN.md step 1): Acts whose text Recourse does not hold. Code spots an Act the person's question NAMES (aliases) or clearly describes (phrases) and says so, with a link to the official text. NOTHING in 'status' or 'appeal' is shown to a user until a person has confirmed it (reviewed); a link is shown only after url_checked is set, otherwise the notice points to the India Code home page. Drafted by Claude from general knowledge and India Code search results; NOT checked by a lawyer.

acts.name: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
acts.url_checked: 2026-10-17 (machine: India Code's own record matches on title, number and year)

status.text: In force. Amended by the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 (from 16 January 2014) and by the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018 (from 26 July 2018).
status.evidence: India Code, read 2026-10-16: the Act's record is not marked repealed; footnotes to sections 13, 15 and 19 cite Act 1 of 2014 (the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013) w.e.f. 16-1-2014; footnotes to sections 4, 7, 13 and others cite Act 16 of 2018 w.e.f. 26-7-2018; India Code's amendment list names the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018.

appeal.text: The High Court has the powers of appeal and revision that the Code of Criminal Procedure gives it, as if the Special Judge's court were a Court of Session (section 27).
appeal.evidence: Section 27 read on India Code 2026-10-16: 'Subject to the provisions of this Act, the High Court may exercise, so far as they may be applicable, all the powers of appeal and revision conferred by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ... on a High Court as if the court of the special Judge were a court of Session ...'.

acts.url_checked: 2026-10-17 (machine: India Code's own record matches on title, number and year)

status.text: In force since 14 November 2012. Amended by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Acts of 2013 and 2018 and by the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act, 2019.
status.evidence: India Code, read 2026-10-16: enforcement date 14-11-2012; not marked repealed; its amendment list names the Criminal Law (Amendment) Acts of 2013 and 2018 and the POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019; footnotes cite Acts 13 of 2013, 22 of 2018 and 25 of 2019.

appeal.text: The Act has no appeal section of its own. A Special Court is a Court of Session and the Code of Criminal Procedure applies to its proceedings (sections 28 and 31), so an appeal from its judgment goes to the High Court as for any Sessions Court judgment.
appeal.evidence: Sections 28 and 31 read on India Code 2026-10-16; no section of the Act mentions an appeal. That a conviction by a Sessions Judge with a sentence above seven years is appealed to the High Court is BNSS section 415(2), read in the library text; for earlier offences the old Code's corresponding section applies (Claude's recollection).

status.text: In force. Amended several times, including by Act 29 of 2004, Act 35 of 2008, Act 3 of 2013 (the 2012 Amendment Act) and Act 28 of 2019 (from 14 August 2019).

appeal.text: Where the trial is before a Special Court under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 (the UAPA's own definition of 'court' includes such a Special Court, section 2(1)(d)), an appeal lies from its judgment, sentence or order (other than an interlocutory order) to the High Court, on facts and on law, within 30 days (the High Court may allow up to 90), under section 21 of that Act. An order of forfeiture under section 26 of the UAPA is appealed to the High Court within one month (section 28).
appeal.evidence: UAPA sections 2(1)(d), 26 and 28 and NIA Act section 21 read on India Code 2026-10-16.

appeal.text: An order of the Adjudicating Authority is appealed to the Appellate Tribunal within 45 days (section 26); an order of the Appellate Tribunal is appealed to the High Court within 60 days (section 42). A Special Court is deemed a Court of Session and the Code of Criminal Procedure applies to its proceedings (sections 44 and 46), so an appeal from a Special Court's judgment goes to the High Court as for any Sessions Court judgment.
appeal.evidence: Sections 26, 42, 44 and 46 read on India Code 2026-10-16. The last step (an appeal from a Special Court's judgment goes to the High Court) follows from section 46 and BNSS section 415(2); it is not stated in the Act.

acts.name: The Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987
aliases: terrorist and disruptive activities prevention act
acts.url_checked: 2026-10-17 (machine: India Code's own record matches on title, number and year)

status.text: No longer in force: India Code lists it as repealed by Act 30 of 2001, and it had ceased to operate earlier, in May 1995. As enacted it was to remain in force for two years from 24 May 1987 (section 1(4)); later amendments extended that. Section 1(4) saved things done, rights acquired and proceedings begun before it ended.
status.evidence: India Code's archive entry reads '(Rep., Act 30 of 2001)'. Section 1(4) read in India Code's PDF of the Act as enacted (two years from the 24th day of May, 1987; savings for rights, penalties and legal proceedings). India Code lists the Amendment Acts of 1985, 1989, 1991 and 1993. The May 1995 date and the length of the extensions are Claude's recollection, not read.

appeal.text: As enacted, section 19 gave an appeal as of right from any judgment, sentence or order (other than an interlocutory order) of a Designated Court directly to the Supreme Court, on facts and on law, within 30 days; no other appeal or revision lay.
appeal.evidence: Section 19 read in India Code's PDF of the Act as enacted (2026-10-16). Later amendments to section 19, if any, were not checked.
